description:
Delete all versions of a local catalog product using product_ref_id from
catalog_list_products. Also removes exclusively used programs, hardware, applications,
sections, manufacturers and stored archives. This is irreversible with project_undo.
Returns {product_ref_id, removed_programs, removed_applications, removed_hardware,
removed_sections, removed_manufacturers, removed_files, affected_devices}. The removed lists
contain IDs, except removed_files contains filenames. affected_devices counts open-project
devices that cannot be loaded until the product is reimported; hardware is unchanged.
name: catalog_delete_product

description:
Find device documentation for a topic such as "dimming curve". Supply product_ref_id
from catalog_list_products to resolve product details, or pass manufacturer directly.
Returns {query, manufacturer, order_number, document_url, references, note}; each reference
has {title, kind, url} and optionally hint.

document_url is a best-effort manual link and may be null. Try it with catalog_docs_fetch,
verify the exact order number and series/generation, then use references as fallbacks.
Read only relevant sections (manuals are often large PDFs). The references are ordered
best-source-first and are fallbacks for each other (manufacturer site / KNX device database /
web search); if none is fetchable, ask the user to open a link and paste the relevant section
rather than guessing. For configuration IDs and allowed values, use
project_list_parameters/project_list_com_objects.
name: catalog_docs

description:
List documentation files cached on the editor host. Returns {items, count}; each item has
{filename, url, size_bytes}. Pass url to catalog_docs_fetch to reuse a PDF or text/Markdown
file offline without searching or downloading again.
name: catalog_docs_cached

description:
Read a PDF or text/Markdown manual incrementally using a URL from catalog_docs. Verify
the device's exact order number and series. GitHub blob URLs become raw-file URLs; downloads
use allowed documentation hosts. Files are cached on disk; refresh=true downloads again.

PDF results always include {url, total_pages}, plus:
- page=N (1-based, takes precedence over find): {page, text, truncated}.
- find="term": {find, pages}, with matching 1-based page numbers.
- neither: {outline, hint}; outline entries have {title, page}, or the list is empty.

Text/Markdown results always include {url, content_type: "text", total_chars}; page is ignored.
- find="term": adds {find, match_count, matches}; matches has at most 50 {line, text} entries
  with 1-based line numbers and snippets up to 200 characters; match_count counts all matches.
- no find: adds {outline, text, truncated, hint}; outline entries have {level, title, line}.

max_chars caps returned page/document text. find is a case-insensitive substring search;
try German/English terms when needed. Use find when a PDF has no outline. Returns the source
url for verification; this does not change the project.
name: catalog_docs_fetch

description:
Download and import online products into the local catalog. catalog_item_ids must be a
nonempty list of id values from downloadable catalog_online_items entries. Omitted or empty
language_ids uses the languages of catalog_online_language; otherwise use codes such as
"de-DE".
Returns {added_refs, added_versions}; added_refs lists distinct product refs for added versions;
each added_versions item has {product_ref_id, hardware2program_ref_id, application_id,
application_version}. Pass product_ref_id and optional hardware2program_ref_id to
project_add_device. The import is outside project_undo history and does not program devices.
name: catalog_download_online_products

description:
Resolve a catalog application by `application_id` (from a catalog_list_products item's
`application_id`). Returns {id, name}.
name: catalog_get_application

description:
Import a .knxprod at path on the editor host into the local catalog, keeping existing
versions. For a file on a remote client, use catalog_import_knxprod_bytes.
Returns {added_refs, added_versions}: added_refs lists distinct product refs for added versions;
each added_versions item has {product_ref_id, hardware2program_ref_id, application_id,
application_version}. Pass product_ref_id and optional hardware2program_ref_id to
project_add_device. Catalog imports are outside project_undo history and do not program
devices.
name: catalog_import_knxprod

description:
Import a .knxprod from a remote client: pass its filename and base64 bytes as data_base64
(decoded size at most 25 MB). Prefer catalog_import_knxprod for files on the editor host.
Returns {added_refs, added_versions, filename, size_bytes}; filename is sanitized and
size_bytes is the decoded size. added_refs lists distinct product refs for added versions;
each added_versions item has {product_ref_id, hardware2program_ref_id, application_id,
application_version}. Pass product_ref_id and optional hardware2program_ref_id to
project_add_device. This changes the local catalog, outside project_undo history.
name: catalog_import_knxprod_bytes

description:
List local catalog product versions. name_contains matches product names/order numbers;
manufacturer_contains matches manufacturer names. Both filters are case-insensitive.
Returns {items, count}; each item has {product_ref_id, hardware2program_ref_id, name,
order_number, application_id, application_version, manufacturer_id, manufacturer_name}.
Pass product_ref_id and optional hardware2program_ref_id to project_add_device; pass
application_id to catalog_get_application. Filter large catalogs to limit the response.
name: catalog_list_products

description:
List a manufacturer's online catalog products over the network. Pass id from
catalog_refresh_online_manufacturers as manufacturer_id. Returns {items, count}; each item
has {id, name, order_number, downloadable}. Collect id values from downloadable items into
catalog_item_ids for catalog_download_online_products.
name: catalog_online_items

description:
Return {language, languages}: the languages online products are downloaded in, the
editor's language first (e.g. "de-DE"), then its other languages.
name: catalog_online_language

description:
Refresh the online manufacturer list over the network. Returns {items, count}; each item
has {id, name}. Pass id as manufacturer_id to catalog_online_items.
name: catalog_refresh_online_manufacturers

description:
Download online products in code only (such as "de-DE") for the rest of the session,
instead of the editor's languages. Returns {language}, containing code. This setting is
outside project_undo history.
name: catalog_set_online_language

description:
Write the device's project individual address to the single device currently in
programming mode. Needs an open connection and an unused project address set beforehand with
project_set_individual_address (this does not check address occupancy); exactly one device
must be in programming mode. This bus change is NOT undoable. ``timeout`` in seconds.

It runs in the editor's operations queue, labelled MCP, like connection_program_device with
scope INDIVIDUAL_ADDRESS: it waits until a device is in programming mode (its programming
button pressed), up to ``timeout``, and the user can cancel it. Returns
{status, node_id, address}.
name: connection_assign_individual_address

description:
Persist the gateway/connection settings. Empty or whitespace-only ``controller_ip`` /
``multicast_group`` strings keep their previous value; non-empty strings replace them.
``routing`` here is only the stored preference — connection_connect always uses tunnelling,
connection_connect_gateway prefers tunnelling and otherwise routing. Disconnect before
changing an active connection's target.
name: connection_configure

description: Connect using the configured gateway IP (tunneling). Waits until connected or fails.
name: connection_connect

description: Connect to a discovered gateway by IP (run connection_scan first). Waits for the result.
name: connection_connect_gateway

description: Disconnect from the bus. Returns the resulting connection state.
name: connection_disconnect

description:
Preview what a download would change on an ALREADY-programmed device, without changing it.

Reads the live device point-to-point and diffs it against the generated image. Needs an open
connection and the device answering at its project individual address — a device that does not
respond (e.g. a virgin/unprogrammed one) fails, so skip this and program a NEW device directly
with scope FULL. ``scope`` defaults to FULL; the individual-address scopes are rejected.
``timeout`` in seconds.

Returns {node_id, changed_bytes, config_bytes, default_bytes, runtime_bytes, config_locations,
changed_segments, changed_properties, summary}. ``changed_bytes`` is the raw total; it is split
into three classes, and ONLY ``config_bytes`` is a real configuration change you would push:
- config_bytes: bytes carrying a configured parameter value / a property write (flags, tables).
- default_bytes: bytes merely reset to the application default (the device holds an older value)
  — benign.
- runtime_bytes: bytes the device firmware manages itself (e.g. a download counter) — benign,
  and they typically never converge to zero even right after a successful download.
So a non-zero ``changed_bytes`` with ``config_bytes == 0`` (``config_locations == 0``) means the
device already carries the configuration; do not treat that as a pending change. changed_segments/
changed_properties are counts and do not describe unload/restart or address-reset effects.
name: connection_evaluate_device

description:
Download the device (``node_id`` from project_list_devices) onto the bus (``timeout``
seconds). Needs an open connection, a project individual address, and the device physically on
the bus; secure devices need a matching loaded keyring. Bus changes are NOT undoable with
project_undo, and a failure or timeout may leave partial changes.

ALREADY-programmed device: run connection_evaluate_device once to preview the diff, then
program with the scope matching your change. NEW device: assign its address first
(project_set_individual_address, then connection_assign_individual_address with the device in
programming mode), then program with scope FULL.

``scope`` (default FULL) selects which loadable parts run; the procedure may reload/restart
the device, so do not assume only changed bytes are written:
- PARAMETERS: parameter values only.
- GROUP_COMMUNICATION: the group-address link tables (address/association/group-object).
- PARAMETERS_AND_GROUP_COMMUNICATION: both of the above — the scope for a change that touches
  parameters AND links (e.g. changing a push-button function type AND relinking its objects).
- APPLICATION: the complete application load — parameters, com-object table, AND the
  group-address link tables (like FULL, without the standalone address-assignment step).
- FULL: the full application load; for a device not yet answering it can also assign the
  project address first (optionally via ``use_serial_number``).
- UNLOAD: remove the application. UNLOAD_ALL also resets the single device in programming mode
  to 15.15.255 — make sure that is the intended device.
- INDIVIDUAL_ADDRESS: write ONLY the project address to the single device in programming mode
  (waits until its programming button is pressed, up to ``timeout``); refused when another
  device already uses the address. OVERWRITE_INDIVIDUAL_ADDRESS writes it to the device
  currently answering at ``current_address`` (required), switching it to programming mode
  remotely.

``use_serial_number`` addresses the device by its project serial (project_set_serial_number)
instead of programming mode — for INDIVIDUAL_ADDRESS, or a FULL commissioning download of a
device that does not answer at its address yet. A device whose hardware is
NoDownloadWithoutPlugin is refused unless ``without_plugin=true``, set only after the user
explicitly confirmed programming it without the manufacturer's plugin.

The programming runs in the editor's operations queue, labelled MCP: the user sees it there
and in its history, it waits behind operations already queued, and the user can cancel it
(the call then fails with the cancel message). Returns {status, node_id}.
name: connection_program_device

description: Read the individual addresses of devices currently in programming mode (needs a connection).
name: connection_read_programming_mode_devices

description:
Discover KNX gateways on the network (``timeout`` in seconds).

Returns ``{complete, count, gateways}``; ``complete`` is false if the timeout elapsed while a
scan was still running (the gateway list may then be incomplete). Connect with
connection_connect_gateway(ip).
name: connection_scan

description: Current connection state and target.
name: connection_status

description:
List EVERY com-object the device's application DECLARES — a superset of the ones currently
active (project_list_com_objects) — so you can see which objects a function could add before
switching its parameters (for group-address planning). Identify the device by ``node_id`` OR
``device_address`` (an individual address like "1.0.30"); pass exactly one.

Returns {items, count}; each item has {ref_id, number, name, function_text, dpt, object_size}
from the STATIC declaration: names/function texts are templates (no parameter or module
substitution) and ``number`` is the base (a module instance offsets it). This is NOT a
reachability proof — a declared object may never be activatable in a given configuration, and
the parameter values that activate each one are NOT included. For the active, linkable objects
(with db_id/flags) and their links, use project_list_com_objects.
name: find_potential_com_objects

description:
Discard the keyring held in memory. Returns {status: "cleared"}. The source file remains
available for keyring_load; project_undo cannot restore runtime keyring state.
name: keyring_clear

description:
Export the loaded keyring to path on the editor host, re-encrypted and signed under
password with the same key material. Requires a loaded keyring. An existing destination
file is overwritten; this cannot be undone with project_undo. Returns {exported: true, path}.
This writes a file without changing keys on bus devices.
name: keyring_export

description:
Decrypt a .knxkeys file at path on the editor host and replace the keyring held in memory.
Raises on a wrong password or invalid file. Returns {loaded: true, path}. This is runtime
state, outside project_undo history; it is not stored in the project or written to the bus.
name: keyring_load

description:
Return {loaded, path, project} for the in-memory keyring. path is its editor-host source
path or null; project is the project name stored in the keyring, or null.
name: keyring_status

description:
Clear cached latest values and the Group Monitor log; active recording continues.
Returns {status: "cleared"}. Cleared data cannot be restored with project_undo.
name: monitor_clear

description:
Read the cached value last seen on a group-address string such as "1/2/3"; no bus request
is sent. Returns {address, service, timestamp, payload}; service is "Write" or "Response",
timestamp is ISO-formatted, and payload is a raw payload string. Raises if no value was seen;
a cached value may be stale.
name: monitor_latest

description:
Send a GroupValueRead to a group-address string (e.g. "1/2/3") and wait up to timeout
seconds for a fresh value. Requires an open connection; raises on timeout. Any Write or
Response seen on that address since the request can satisfy the wait, including unrelated
traffic. Returns {address, service, timestamp, payload}; timestamp is ISO-formatted and payload
is a raw payload string. This sends a bus read without editing the project.
name: monitor_read_value

description:
Queue a GroupValueRead to a group-address string such as "1/2/3". Requires an open
connection. Returns {status: "queued", address} without waiting for a reply; monitor_read_value
waits for a fresh value. When polling monitor_latest, check timestamp to avoid stale data.
This sends a bus read without editing the project.
name: monitor_send_read

description:
Queue a GroupValueWrite to a group-address string such as "1/2/3". Requires an open
connection. value is encoded using dpt, or the address's project DPT when omitted; missing
or unsupported DPTs and values that cannot be encoded raise an error.
Returns {status: "queued", address}; this does not confirm delivery or device action.
This can actuate hardware and is not reversible with project_undo; it does not edit the
project. Inspect fresh bus feedback to verify the effect.
name: monitor_send_write

description:
Read the Group Monitor's recorded group telegrams, oldest first. limit selects the most
recent entries (<=0 means all). Returns {items, count}; each item has {timestamp, source,
destination, service, payload}. timestamp is ISO-formatted; service is "Read", "Write" or
"Response"; payload is a raw payload string or null for reads. count is the returned count.
name: monitor_telegrams

description:
Read raw cEMI frames from the Group Monitor and Bus Activity, merged oldest first.
limit selects the most recent frames (<=0 means all). Returns {items, count}; each item has
{timestamp, source_type, monitor, msg_code, src_addr, dst_addr, hops, raw}. timestamp is
ISO-formatted, source_type is "connection", monitor is "group_monitor" or "bus_activity",
and raw is space-separated hex. Non-data frames have empty addresses and null hops.
count is the returned count.
name: network_cemi_records

description:
Clear the Group Monitor and Bus Activity logs; active recording continues and cached
latest values remain. Returns {status: "cleared"}. Cleared logs cannot be restored with
project_undo.
name: network_clear

description:
Enable recording in the Group Monitor and Bus Activity for the normal connection.
Existing entries are kept; network_clear clears them. Returns {status: "capturing"}.
This enables local recording without opening a bus connection.
name: network_start

description:
Read recording state for the normal connection's Group Monitor and Bus Activity.
Returns {state, recording, telegrams, cemi_records}; recording has {group_monitor, bus_activity}
booleans, and state is "capturing" while either records, otherwise "stopped". telegrams counts
buffered L_Data frames; cemi_records counts all buffered frames. Recording state does not
establish whether a bus connection is open.
name: network_state

description:
Stop Group Monitor and Bus Activity recording while keeping buffered entries and the
normal bus connection unchanged. Returns {status: "stopped"}.
name: network_stop

description:
Read decoded L_Data telegrams from the Group Monitor and Bus Activity, merged oldest first.
limit selects the most recent decodable entries (<=0 means all). Returns {items, count}; each
item has {timestamp, source_type, monitor, telegram}. timestamp is ISO-formatted, source_type
is "connection", monitor is "group_monitor" or "bus_activity", and telegram is a display
string. count is the returned count.
name: network_telegrams

description:
Add a device to the project using product_ref_id from catalog_list_products.
Optional hardware2program_ref_id from the same catalog listing selects its application;
omitting it selects the newest catalog version. Undoable with project_undo; commissioning
hardware requires separate connection tools.

Returns {node_id, name, individual_address, description}, or only {node_id} if the created
device cannot be loaded. Pass node_id to device tools.
name: project_add_device

description:
Add a KNX Data Secure device certificate: ``code`` is the FDSK from the device label
(36 characters, groups separated by "-"). A device with the certificate's serial number is
then commissioned securely with it. With ``node_id`` or ``device_address`` the certificate is for that device:
one without a serial number takes the certificate's, one with another is refused. Needs a
password-protected project.
name: project_add_device_certificate

description:
Assign the missing additional individual addresses of a project device (the
tunnelling addresses of an IP interface) using node_id or device_address: entries
are created up to count (default: as many as the device's application has) and every
entry without an address gets one, the highest free device numbers of the device's line
counting down from 255. One undo step (project_undo). Fails when the line has too few free
addresses. Returns {node_id, additional_addresses}, each {index, address, name,
description}.
name: project_assign_additional_addresses

description:
Apply project edits in order. Each operations entry is {"op": name, "params": {...}}.
These are undoable project steps; applying changes to hardware requires connection tools.
A batch may require multiple project_undo calls. IDs must be known before the call; later
operations cannot reference earlier results.

Device-scoped ops accept either ``node_id`` (int) OR ``device_address`` (str, e.g. "1.0.30");
GA-scoped ops accept either ``group_address_id`` (int) OR ``group_address`` (str, e.g.
"10/1/2"). Pass exactly one of each pair. Below "device" / "ga" stand for either form.

Supported ops with required params (optional params in brackets) and success result fields:
- add_device: product_ref_id [name] -> {node_id}; uses the first matching catalog product.
- rename_device: (node_id | device_address), name -> {node_id, device_address, name}.
- set_individual_address: (node_id | device_address), address -> {node_id, device_address, address}.
- set_parameter: (node_id | device_address), (parameter_ref_id | label [channel] [subtree_id tree_token] [value_label]),
  value? -> {node_id, device_address, ref_id, requested, value, active, changed?, lost_links?, activated_com_objects, unlocked_parameters}.
  Address the parameter by parameter_ref_id, or semantically by label (resolved AT THIS OP'S TURN within channel or subtree_id,
  so a child a prior op in the batch just activated resolves; channel scopes by name e.g. 'A' without needing tree_token;
  value_label gives an enum's value). value is read back after the edit; changed lists
  calculated side effects; lost_links lists links a function/mode change dropped.
- set_com_object_flag: (node_id | device_address), com_object_ref_id, flag, value -> {node_id, device_address, com_object_ref_id}.
- create_group_address: [address, name] -> {group_address_id}.
- rename_group_address: (group_address_id | group_address), name -> {group_address_id, group_address, name}.
- set_group_address_dpt: (group_address_id | group_address) [dpt; omitted/null clears] -> {group_address_id, group_address, dpt}.
- remove_group_address: (group_address_id | group_address) -> {group_address_id, group_address}.
- link_com_object: (node_id | device_address), com_object_ref_id, (group_address_id | group_address) [is_sending=false] ->
  {link_id, node_id, device_address, com_object_ref_id, com_object_db_id, group_address_id, group_address, is_sending,
  already_linked, dpt_mismatch?, other_sending_group_address_ids?} (same feedback as the
  standalone tool; idempotent).
- unlink_com_object: assignment_id | ((node_id | device_address), com_object_ref_id, (group_address_id | group_address)) -> {assignment_id}.
- create_area: area_number [name] -> {area_id}.
- create_line: area_id, line_number [name] -> {line_id}.

Use node_id from project_list_devices, product_ref_id from catalog_list_products, parameter
ref_id from project_list_parameters as parameter_ref_id, and object ref_id from
project_list_com_objects as com_object_ref_id. Use id from project_create_group_address or
project_get_group_address as group_address_id; use area id from project_topology as area_id. For assignment_id, use id
from project_get_ga_assignments, assignment_id from project_get_com_object_links or a returned
link_id. Linkable objects are required for linking; set is_sending=true for a transmitting
link. flag is communication/read/write/transmit/update/read_on_init.

dry_run=true checks only operation names, required params and flag names, without applying
edits or validating referenced entities/values. Returns {dry_run, valid, results}; each result
has {index, op, valid}, plus issue when invalid. index is zero-based.

deferred=true (default) enables multi-pass deferred validation: operations that fail because
a prerequisite (e.g. parent switch activating a child parameter, or a function activating a
com-object) has not yet run in the batch are deferred and retried in subsequent passes once
other operations succeed. Setting deferred=false enforces strict single-pass order.

With dry_run=false, returns {applied, atomic, rolled_back, ok, failed, results}. Each result
has {index, op, status}, plus result on "ok" or error on "error"; "skipped" has neither.
atomic=true (default) stops on the first unresolvable error and rewinds applied project edits;
later operations are skipped. atomic=false continues, so applied=true can coexist with
failures. ok counts successful handler returns even after rollback; inspect rolled_back and
each result. Handlers can return without changing anything, so re-read critical edits.
name: project_batch

description:
Change a device's project application to another program of its hardware. Use node_id
or device_address and hardware2program_ref_id from project_list_application_programs
for that device. Parameters, group-object links and flags reset to the new application's
defaults; address, name and serial number stay.

Undoable with project_undo. Apply it on the bus with connection_program_device(scope="FULL").
Returns {node_id, application_id, version, note}.
name: project_change_application

description:
Close the open project. Returns {status: "closed"}. Reopen it with project_open;
closing is outside project_undo history.
name: project_close

description:
Remove product data no device uses from the open project and compact its file.

dry_run=true (default) previews removal and estimates file_size_after. Applying compaction
is irreversible with project_undo; removed product data must be imported again if needed.
Returns {status, nothing_unused, file_size_before, file_size_after, removed,
product_data_size_before, product_data_size_after}; sizes are bytes. status is "analysed" or
"compacted". removed contains lists named application_programs, products, hardware,
catalog_items, baggages and manufacturers: IDs, except baggages contains archive paths.
name: project_compact

description:
Compare two devices (by node_id or device_address) across header, parameters and
com-objects. Items are keyed so two instances of the SAME application line up (parameters by
application-relative ref, com-objects by object number). Returns {node_id_a, node_id_b,
difference_count, header, parameters, com_objects}; each section is a list of rows
{key, label, kind, a, b} where kind is added|removed|changed|same and a/b are the values on
each device ("" when the item is absent there). Com-object rows additionally carry
a_links/b_links: the group addresses each device links as [{address, sending}] (sending
first). This lets a caller tell a structural difference (object linked on one side only, or
different flags/DPT) from a mere room-mapped GA difference (same structure, both linked
sending, only the address differs). With only_differences=true (default) the 'same' rows are
omitted to keep the result small.
name: project_compare_devices

description:
Create a project topology area. Undoable with project_undo.
Returns {area_id, area_number, name}; use area_id for project_create_line and area edits.
name: project_create_area

description:
Create a single project group address (low-level fallback; prefer project_batch to create GAs and link atomically). address follows project_info's group_address_style
(e.g. "1/2/3"); omit it for the next free address. Returns {group_address_id, address, name},
or only {group_address_id} if the created row cannot be read. Pass group_address_id to group
address and linking tools. Undoable with project_undo; hardware changes require linking
com-objects and programming their devices.
name: project_create_group_address

description:
Create a project topology line. Use an area's id from project_topology as area_id.
Undoable with project_undo. Returns {line_id, area_id, line_number}; pass line_id to line edits.
name: project_create_line

description:
Create a building/location space. ``space_type`` is one of Building, BuildingPart, Floor,
Room, Corridor, Stairway, DistributionBoard. ``parent_id`` is a parent space ``id`` from
project_spaces (null = top level). Undoable project edit. Returns {space_id, parent_id,
space_type, name}.
name: project_create_space

description:
List devices that project_update_application can update: the local catalog has a
version of the same application program whose ReplacesVersions names the current one.

Returns {items, count}; each item has {node_id, individual_address, name, application_id,
current_version, available_version}. Pass an item's node_id to project_update_application
to update the project; this lookup does not change the project or bus.
name: project_devices_with_update

description:
Show changes made in the current session (dirty state since opening/saving),
OR compare the current project against an external project file (.knxproj or .xknx).

compare_against.description:
Optional path to a .knxproj or .xknx file. If omitted,
             diffs the current uncommitted session edits against the open project baseline.

only_differences.description: If True (default), omits unchanged elements to keep the diff concise.

name: project_diff

description:
Export the open project's key material as a keyring (``.knxkeys``) to ``dest``,
encrypted with ``password``: the backbone key, the devices commissioned securely, the
tunnels of the KNX IP Secure devices and the keys of the secured group addresses (e.g. for
a secure tunnel of another tool).
name: project_export_keyring

description:
Export the open project to a .knxproj archive at ``dest`` (with manufacturer bundle).
Returns {status, dest} plus an optional ``warning``. ``status="incomplete"`` means
manufacturer references are missing — ETS may reject the archive, so inspect the warning.
name: project_export_knxproj

description:
Scan a multi-channel or modular device (actuators, touch panels, push-buttons, inputs)
for free and used channels, controls, or slots.

Identifies functional slots by inspecting UI containers and primary selector parameters
(e.g. 'Channel function', 'Funktion', 'Betriebsart').

device_address.description: Individual address (e.g. '1.0.30'). Pass exactly one of node_id or device_address.

function_filter.description:
Optional filter to only return slots that currently have, or can be configured to,
             the specified function (e.g. 'Schalten', 'Dimmen', 'Jalousie').

slot_type.description: Optional substring filter on slot name/path (e.g. 'Steuerung', 'Channel', 'Kanal').

name: project_find_free_slots

description:
Read a project com-object. Identify the device by ``node_id`` OR ``device_address`` (an
individual address like "1.0.30"); pass exactly one. Pass the object's ref_id from
project_list_com_objects as com_object_ref_id. Returns {ref_id, db_id, linkable, name, number,
dpt, dpt_name, object_size, flags}; flags contains communication, read, write, transmit,
update, read_on_init. linkable=true is required for linking and flag edits.
name: project_get_com_object

description:
Read a com-object's group-address links in the project. Identify the device by ``node_id``
OR ``device_address`` (an individual address like "1.0.30"); pass exactly one. Pass ref_id
from project_list_com_objects as com_object_ref_id.
Returns {items, count}; each item has {assignment_id, group_address_id, address, name,
is_sending}. Pass assignment_id to project_unlink_com_object. items is empty when the object
is not instantiated or has no links; address and name are null if the group address is absent.
These project links do not verify what is currently programmed on the bus.
name: project_get_com_object_links

description:
Read a project device. Identify it by ``node_id`` OR ``device_address`` (an individual
address like "1.0.30"); pass exactly one. Returns {node_id, name, individual_address,
description}, plus {product_ref_id, hardware2program_ref_id, order_number, hardware_name,
product_name, manufacturer_name, additional_addresses} when catalog metadata is available.
individual_address is null when unset. additional_addresses lists the device's additional
individual addresses (the tunnelling addresses of an IP interface) as {index, address, name,
description}; index is 1-based (the AddressIndex of a tunnelling interface), address an
"a.l.d" string or null for an entry without one.
name: project_get_device

description:
Read a group address's project com-object links using group_address_id or group_address string
(e.g. '10/1/2'). Returns {items, count}; each item has {id, com_object_db_id, group_address_id,
is_sending, node_id, individual_address, com_object_ref_id, com_object_name}.
name: project_get_ga_assignments

description:
Read a project group address using group_address_id or group_address string (e.g. '10/1/2').
Returns {id, address, name, datapoint_type, description, data_secure}.
name: project_get_group_address

description:
The KNX IP Secure settings of a secure IP device commissioned securely: whether its
tunnels are secured and its bus interfaces (kind, user id, tunnelling address). With
``include_passwords`` also its commissioning password, its authentication code and the
bus interfaces' passwords - only when the user asks for them.
name: project_get_ip_secure

description:
Read a project application parameter. Identify the device by ``node_id`` OR
``device_address`` (an individual address like "1.0.30"); pass exactly one. Identify the parameter
by ``parameter_ref_id`` OR semantically by ``path`` (e.g. "Steuerung 1 / Funktion") or ``label``.
Returns {ref_id, label, value, default_value, access, widget}; for an enum, widget includes
the full ``choices`` (value/label/id) — the allowed values for project_set_parameter.
name: project_get_parameter

description:
Project edit history. Returns {items, count}; each item has {id, label, reverted}. Pass an
item's ``id`` as project_jump_to's ``event_id``.
name: project_history

description:
Import a .knxproj (``source``) into a new .xknx project at ``dest`` and open it.

Both paths are on the editor host. ``password`` is required for encrypted projects; it
then protects the new project too. An archive with KNX Secure data but without a password
needs ``project_password`` to protect the new project. An existing file at ``dest`` is
replaced and bundled product data is imported into the local catalog; neither the file
replacement nor the catalog import is undoable with project_undo. Returns {open, path}.
name: project_import_knxproj

description:
Project metadata. Returns {id, name, group_address_style, guid, created_by, last_modified,
schema_version, tool_version}. ``group_address_style`` (ThreeLevel/TwoLevel/Free) governs how
group-address strings parse.
name: project_info

description:
Move the project undo/redo cursor to a history entry, passing id from project_history as
event_id. This reverts or reapplies project edits; bus changes and file replacements are
outside this history. Returns {status: "jumped", event_id}, with event_id as a string.
name: project_jump_to

description:
Create a single group-object link (low-level fallback; prefer project_batch to create GAs and link objects atomically). The
device is identified by ``node_id`` (from project_list_devices) OR ``device_address`` (an
individual address like "1.0.30"); the group address by ``group_address_id`` (from
project_create_group_address or project_get_group_address) OR ``group_address`` (a printed address like "10/1/2" in the
project's style). Pass exactly one of each pair. ``com_object_ref_id`` is the object's
``ref_id`` from project_list_com_objects (linkable=true).

``is_sending`` (default False) marks which group address an object with SEVERAL links sends to
(it orders the associations, sending GA first); it does NOT change the object's flags, and for
a single link it has no byte effect — the send/receive direction comes from the object's own
flags. For a transmitting object (push-button/sensor output) linked to several GAs, mark its
intended sending GA; keep one sending GA per object. Returns {link_id, node_id,
com_object_ref_id, com_object_db_id, group_address_id, is_sending, already_linked} plus, when
relevant, ``dpt_mismatch`` ({com_object, group_address} — the GA keeps its own DPT, so the
DPT metadata differs; verify compatibility) and ``other_sending_group_address_ids`` (the
object already sends to these, so it now has several sending GAs). Linking the same pair again
is idempotent (``already_linked: true``, no duplicate). Pass link_id as
project_unlink_com_object's assignment_id. Program the device to apply the link on the bus.
name: project_link_com_object

description:
The application programs a device can be changed to with project_change_application:
the other programs of its hardware in the local catalog, older and newer.

Use node_id from project_list_devices or device_address. Returns {items, count}; each item has
{hardware2program_ref_id, application_id, name, version}. Pass hardware2program_ref_id to
project_change_application for the same device. This lookup is read-only.
name: project_list_application_programs

description:
List a project device's visible com-objects. Identify the device by ``node_id`` OR
``device_address`` (an individual address like "1.0.30"); pass exactly one.
Returns {items, count}; each item has {ref_id, db_id, linkable, name, number, dpt, dpt_name,
object_size, flags}. flags contains communication, read, write, transmit, update, read_on_init.
Pass ref_id as com_object_ref_id with the same device. Linking and flag edits require
linkable=true (db_id set).
name: project_list_com_objects

description:
List project devices, optionally filtering names by a case-insensitive substring.
Returns {items, count}; each item has {node_id, name, individual_address, description}.
Pass node_id to device tools; individual_address is null when unset. This reads the project.
name: project_list_devices

description:
List visible parameters (to discover free channels/functions on multi-channel devices, prefer project_find_free_slots). Identify the
device by ``node_id`` OR ``device_address`` (an individual address like "1.0.30"); pass
exactly one.
Returns {items, count}; each item has ref_id, label, value, default_value, access, widget.
To keep the list compact, an enum ``widget`` carries only ``choice_count`` (plus
``value_label`` on the item for the current value), NOT the full choice list — call
project_get_parameter for a single parameter's complete ``choices``.

Filters:
- ``search`` / ``query``: filters by substring match on label (case-insensitive).
- ``channel``: filters parameters by channel or section (e.g. 'A', 'Kanal A', '1').
- ``modified_only``: if True, returns only parameters whose current value differs from default.
- ``compact``: if True, returns a lightweight dictionary omitting schema details and choice lists.

Pass an item's ``ref_id`` to project_set_parameter as its ``parameter_ref_id`` argument.
name: project_list_parameters

description:
Move a space under a different parent space, or to the top level with new_parent_id=null.
Both ``id`` values come from project_spaces. Undoable project edit. Returns
{space_id, new_parent_id}.
name: project_move_space

description:
Create a new empty KNX project (.xknx) at ``path`` (on the editor host) and open it. An
existing file at ``path`` is replaced and the current project closed; file replacement is NOT
undoable with project_undo. Returns {open, path}.
name: project_new

description:
Return {address} for the next unused project group address, formatted per project_info's
group_address_style. This does not reserve it or check the bus. Pass address to
project_create_group_address to create it.
name: project_next_free_group_address

description:
Open an existing .xknx project at path on the editor host, closing the current project.
Returns {open, path}. Switching projects is outside project_undo history.

``password`` is required for a password-protected project.
name: project_open

description:
Read a device's nested parameter UI. Identify the device by ``node_id`` OR
``device_address`` (an individual address like "1.0.30"); pass exactly one. Group
headings distinguish repeated labels for different channels, buttons or display levels.
Returns {items, count, outline, tree_token}; count is the number of top-level nodes. Node
fields depend on kind:
- "tab"/"block": {kind, id, name, children, ref?}, with children using the same node shapes.
  ``id`` is a UNIQUE index path (pass it verbatim as ``subtree_id``); ``ref`` is the raw
  module/block id, which REPEATS across module instances and must not be used to address one.
- "parameter": {kind, ref_id, label, value, default_value, access, widget}.
- "button": {kind, id, text, online, read_only}; other nodes contain only kind.
To stay compact, an enum ``widget`` here carries only ``choice_count`` (plus ``value_label``
for the current value), NOT the full choice list — call project_get_parameter for one
parameter's complete ``choices``.

The response also carries ``outline`` (bool). On a LARGE device a plain call
(no ``outline``/``subtree_id``) returns the outline automatically instead of a huge tree —
then ``outline`` is true and ``parameter_count`` gives the full size. To avoid pulling a big
tree whole:
- ``outline=True`` returns ONLY the container skeleton — each tab/block as
  {kind, id, name, parameter_count, com_object_count, children} with no parameter/com-object
  leaves. Read this to see the structure and pick a section.
- ``subtree_id="<id>"`` returns only that one tab/block's subtree (optionally also with
  ``outline=True``). Scoped reads REQUIRE ``tree_token`` from the SAME read the id came
  from — a path can keep existing after a structural change but point to a different
  container, and the token detects that. A stale token raises; re-read without the subtree
  to get a fresh one. project_list_parameters(search=...) finds a parameter by label.
- ``tree_token`` is a short fingerprint of the device's current structure. Pass it back to
  any scoped read/mutation (``subtree_id``, project_resolve_parameter, batch set_parameter)
  to prove the structure has not changed since the id was obtained.

Pass a parameter's ref_id as parameter_ref_id to project_get_parameter/project_set_parameter.
This reads project configuration.
name: project_parameter_tree

description: Redo the last undone project edit. Returns {redone: bool}.
name: project_redo

description:
Remove a project topology area and its lines/devices. Use an area's id from
project_topology as area_id. Undoable with project_undo; hardware is unchanged.
Returns {status: "removed", area_id}, with area_id as a string.
name: project_remove_area

description: Remove a group address and its links (low-level fallback; prefer project_batch with op="remove_group_address"). Uses group_address_id or group_address string.
name: project_remove_group_address

description:
Remove a project topology line and its devices. Use a line's id from project_topology as
line_id. Undoable with project_undo; hardware is unchanged. Returns {status: "removed", line_id},
with line_id as a string.
name: project_remove_line

description:
Remove a space and its sub-spaces (``id`` from project_spaces); devices placed in them
become unassigned. Undoable project edit. Returns {status, space_id}.
name: project_remove_space

description:
Rename a project topology area, using an area's id from project_topology as area_id.
Undoable with project_undo. Returns {area_id, name}.
name: project_rename_area

description:
Rename a project device using node_id or device_address. Undoable with
project_undo. Returns {node_id, name, individual_address, description}.
name: project_rename_device

description: Rename a project group address using group_address_id or group_address string.
name: project_rename_group_address

description:
Rename a project topology line, using a line's id from project_topology as line_id.
Undoable with project_undo. Returns {line_id, name}.
name: project_rename_line

description:
Rename a space (``id`` from project_spaces). Undoable project edit. Returns
{space_id, name}.
name: project_rename_space

description:
Resolve a parameter by its human ``label`` or hierarchy ``path`` (e.g. "Steuerung 1 / Funktion")
to the ``ref_id`` that project_set_parameter needs, so a caller can avoid the long XML ref ids.
Identify the device by ``node_id`` OR ``device_address`` (an individual address like "1.0.30"); pass exactly one.

``label`` or ``path`` is matched among the device's currently ACTIVE parameters, within an optional scope.
- pass ``path`` (e.g. 'Steuerung 1 / Funktion' or 'Seite 1 / Steuerung 1') to uniquely resolve across identical channel labels;
- pass ``channel`` (e.g. 'A', 'Kanal A', '1') to scope to a channel by name without needing
  index paths or tokens;
- pass ``subtree_id`` (a container ``id`` from project_parameter_tree(outline=True)) to scope
  the match to one channel/block;
- a label that matches several parameters raises with the candidate ref_ids (narrow the
  scope); a label that matches none raises too. It never guesses.
With ``value_label`` (an enum choice's text) the result also carries ``resolved_value``, the
raw value to pass to project_set_parameter.

Returns {ref_id, label, value, access, resolved_value?, channel?, path?}.
name: project_resolve_parameter

description:
Set an additional individual address of a project device (a tunnelling address of an
IP interface) using node_id or device_address. index is 1-based (see
additional_addresses in project_get_device; entries up to it are created). address is an
"a.l.d" string in the device's own line, or a device number 1-255; null or "" clears it.
It must not be used by a device or another additional address of the line. name and
description, when given, are set too. Each change is one undo step (project_undo).
Returns {node_id, additional_addresses}. This does not write the bus; a full download of
the device writes the addresses.
name: project_set_additional_address

description:
Override a com-object flag (low-level fallback; prefer project_batch with op="set_com_object_flag").
Pass ref_id from project_list_com_objects as com_object_ref_id with node_id or device_address;
the object must have linkable=true. Undoable with project_undo; program the device to apply
the change on the bus.

Returns {ref_id, db_id, linkable, name, number, dpt, dpt_name, object_size, flags}, or only
{ref_id} if the updated object cannot be found. flags contains the six named flags.
name: project_set_com_object_flag

description:
Place a device in a room/space, or remove it from any space with space_id=null. Accepts
node_id or device_address, and a space id from project_spaces. Undoable project
edit. Returns {node_id, device_address, space_id}.
name: project_set_device_space

description:
Set a project group address's datapoint type, or clear it with dpt=null, using group_address_id
or group_address string (e.g. '10/1/2').
name: project_set_group_address_dpt

description: Set a group address' KNX Data Secure mode using group_address_id or group_address string.
name: project_set_group_address_security

description:
Set a project device's individual address, e.g. "1.1.5", using node_id or device_address.
The target area/line must exist in project_topology and the address
must be unused in the project. Returns {node_id, name, individual_address, description}.
Undoable with project_undo. This does not check or write the bus; use
connection_assign_individual_address to assign it to hardware.
name: project_set_individual_address

description:
Change a secure IP device's KNX IP Secure settings (the next download writes them):
its commissioning password, its authentication code, the password of one bus interface
(``interface_ref_id`` from project_get_ip_secure) or whether its tunnels are secured.
Passwords have 1 to 20 Latin-1 characters.
name: project_set_ip_secure

description:
Set a single application parameter (low-level fallback; prefer project_setup_parameters to auto-activate gating selectors). Identify the device by ``node_id`` OR ``device_address`` (an
individual address like "1.0.30"); pass exactly one. Pass the parameter's `ref_id` (from
project_list_parameters, or project_parameter_tree) as the `parameter_ref_id` argument; use a
`value` permitted by that parameter's `widget`.

Alternatively, use semantic addressing: pass `path` (e.g. 'Steuerung 1 / Funktion') or `label`
(with optional `channel`, `path` or `subtree_id` scope) instead of `parameter_ref_id`, and
`value_label` (an enum choice's text) instead of raw `value`.

When you configure a device's push-button / display function (e.g. a glass push button, room
controller), ALWAYS also set its display symbols and key labels/name — do not leave them at
their defaults.

Returns {ref_id, requested, value, active, changed?, lost_links?, activated_com_objects, unlocked_parameters}:
``value`` is read back AFTER the edit (may be a normalized form of ``requested``, or null with ``active=false`` if
the edit deactivated the parameter), ``changed`` lists other parameters a calculation changed
as a side effect, ``lost_links`` lists group-address links this change dropped by
deactivating their com-objects ({com_object_ref_id, group_address_id, address}),
``activated_com_objects`` lists com-objects newly visible after this edit, and
``unlocked_parameters`` lists parameters newly active after this edit. A rejected
value raises with the reason and does NOT take effect on a later edit.
name: project_set_parameter

description:
Activate or deactivate a KNX Data Secure device's secure commissioning (one undo step).
Accepts node_id or device_address. Activated, the device gets a Tool Key (needs a password-protected
project) and is commissioned with its device certificate. Deactivated, it is programmed in the clear: its
"Auto" group addresses communicate in the clear and its links to group addresses with
Security "On" are removed (the result lists both).
name: project_set_secure_commissioning

description:
Store a device's KNX serial number in the project using node_id or device_address.
serial_number takes 12 hex digits (e.g. "0083:7AA2039C"); an empty string clears it.
Returns {node_id, serial_number}. Undoable with project_undo; this records metadata without
writing hardware. connection_program_device can use it with use_serial_number=true.
name: project_set_serial_number

description:
Set a space's type (Building, BuildingPart, Floor, Room, Corridor, Stairway,
DistributionBoard). ``id`` from project_spaces. Undoable project edit. Returns
{space_id, space_type}.
name: project_set_space_type

description:
Setup and configure parameters on a device, automatically resolving and enabling
any required parent selector gates (Choose/When dependency chains) in the activation path.

This eliminates manual discovery and sequential toggling of gating switches when configuring
nested functions (e.g. channel mode, push-button actions, rocker settings). Each entry in
``parameters`` specifies:
- target: ``ref_id``, ``path`` (e.g. 'Steuerung 1 / Funktion'), or ``label``
- value: ``value`` (raw value) or ``value_label`` (enum choice text)

If the target parameter is gated behind parent Choose/When conditions that are not yet active,
the activation path is resolved, parent selector parameters are scheduled with satisfying values,
and all edits are applied atomically in one transaction.

Returns {status, planned_edits, applied, changed, activated_com_objects, unlocked_parameters}.
If dry_run is True, returns planned_edits without applying the changes.
name: project_setup_parameters

description:
Read the building/location tree (building -> floor -> room), each with its placed devices
and functions. Use this to find a room's devices when device names are empty — the space names
carry the location. Returns {items, count, unassigned_devices}; count counts top-level nodes.
Each space has {id, name, space_type, number, usage_text, description, devices, functions,
children}; a device has {node_id, name, individual_address, description, product_name,
manufacturer_name} (pass node_id to device tools). unassigned_devices lists devices placed in
no space. Pass a space's id as project_set_device_space's space_id.
name: project_spaces

description:
Return {open, path}, with the editor-host path or null when no project is open.
Most project_* tools need an open project.
name: project_status

description:
Read the project topology. Returns {items, count}; each area item has
{id, area_number, name, lines}, and each line has {id, line_number, name}. count counts areas.
Pass an area's id as area_id and a line's id as line_id to topology tools; these IDs differ
from the area/line numbers used in individual addresses.
name: project_topology

description:
Undo the last undoable project edit. Returns {undone: bool}. Bus programming, address
assignment, and file replacements are outside project history and are not reverted.
name: project_undo

description:
Remove a group-object link (low-level fallback; prefer project_batch with op="unlink_com_object"). Remove by ``assignment_id``, OR directly by specifying
``node_id``/``device_address``, ``com_object_ref_id``, and ``group_address_id``/``group_address``.
name: project_unlink_com_object

description:
Update a device to the local catalog version of the SAME application program that
replaces the current one ("Update Application Program Version"). Parameter values carry over
by ParameterRef number, group objects of the same size by ComObjectRef number with their
flags, priority, datapoint type and group-address links.

This is an undoable project edit (project_undo). To apply it on the bus, program the device
afterwards with connection_program_device and scope="FULL". Returns {node_id, new_version,
kept, dropped, note}; kept and dropped are counts of carried-over vs discarded parameters and
group objects.
name: project_update_application

description:
One-call overview: project, connection, keyring, capture state, plus valid enums.

Call this first. ``capabilities`` lists the download scopes, com-object flags, and (when a
project is open) the group-address style that other tools accept.
name: status
